title: Public images, custom images and machine families with a GPU

videos.script: Every machine boots from an image. This lesson is about where images come from, and which one you actually get. {{projects}} The public ones live in projects of their own. Debian lives in debian-cloud. You point at it by name, and you never upload it. {{family}} Most images belong to a family. A family points to its newest image that is not deprecated. That pointer moves while you are not looking, which is good for patches and bad for twins. {{own}} Then your own images. You set a machine up once, stop it, and copy its disk. Every machine made from that copy starts the same. {{gpu}} Last, the machines with a GPU. The card is in one host and cannot move with the machine. So these machines stop for maintenance, they cost ten times more, and the quota starts at zero.
